State party president Govind Singh Dotasra dismissed claims of discord, attributing them to BJP propaganda.
title: 'Better to die with self-respect': Ex-maharaja of Bharatpur Vishvendra Singh quits Cong

author: DHRUV YADAV
description: Nations are increasingly ordering fourth- and 4.5-generation fighters as they are cost-effective and readily available. France's Rafale and the US F-15EX are prominent examples of this trend. Various countries, including Ukraine and Colombia, have made commitments to acquire these aircraft. Fourth-generation fighters remain effective with capabilities that complement fifth-generation fighters. Their operational advantages indicate that they will continue to play a significant role in air forces.
title: Rafale, F-15EX & Gripen: Why 4th gen jets are bagging billion-dollar orders in age of 6th-gen

author: TOI TECH DESK
description: Jamie Dimon has advocated for a groundbreaking free-trade agreement between the United States and Europe to boost economic progress. He insists Europe must implement essential economic and military reforms to enhance competitiveness. Dimon envisions that a united front among democratic nations can effectively tackle geopolitical challenges and establish global trade benchmarks while simultaneously strengthening the American economy and democratic partnerships.
title: Jamie Dimon warns Europe again: 'You may be losing,' offers a solution

author: TOI
description: Russia became an unusually attractive supplier when Western buyers retreated after the war with Ukraine. Its share of Indian crude imports, below 2% before the war, expanded rapidly as discounts compensated refiners for longer supply chains. In the present day, the situation has become more complex, the new US law potentially changes the economics of India’s Russian oil purchases.
title: Will Russian oil be economically viable for India if Trump tariffs return?

author: AASTHA JHA
title: 'Terrorist act': UAE official on flydubai attack, praises India pilot Smit Machchhar

author: TOI ENTERTAINMENT DESK
description: The Economic Offences Wing has summoned Dino Morea to discuss his connections to the alleged Mithi River desilting scam. Notably, phone records suggest he may have communicated with key individuals tied to the case. His brother, Santino Rocco Morea, is also being questioned. The inquiry aims to reveal any possible financial irregularities related to municipal contracts, as the agency explores the broader implications of this developing scandal.
title: Dino Morea summoned again by EOW in Mithi River desilting case

author: TOI ENTERTAINMENT DESK
description: Thalapathy Vijay's son, Jason Sanjay, steps into direction with his debut film 'Sigma'. This thrilling heist drama, starring Sundeep Kishan, has drawn a mix of enthusiastic and lukewarm reactions from audiences. With an opening day box office earning of approximately Rs. 1.08 crore, many praised Kishan's acting, although some viewers found the plot to be somewhat predictable. The film released in both Tamil and Telugu languages, boosting its overall earnings.
title: ‘Sigma’ BO day 1: Jason Sanjay-Sundeep Kishan starrer begins its theatrical run

author: AADRITA HALDER
title: Gujarat UCC Bill gets President Murmu’s nod paving way for implementation

author: TOI WORLD DESK
description: Cory Mohl from West Valley City has constructed a remarkable backyard railroad project, aiming to share his love for trains with the community. He dedicated significant time and resources to build around 400 feet of track, attracting local children who delight in riding the miniature train. This charming setup has become a beloved neighborhood fixture, encouraging connections among residents.
title: Utah man built backyard railroad with 40,000 pounds of gravel and $18,000 budget

author: TOI WORLD DESK
description: Kevin O’Leary-backed plans for a 40,000-acre AI data centre district in Utah have been cut to about 20,000 acres after strong local opposition. Residents have raised concerns over the project’s energy and water use, environmental impact and public review. Developers say the project could create thousands of jobs and support US computing and national defence.
title: Kevin O’Leary-backed Utah AI data center plan downsized after local backlash

author: TOI REAL ESTATE DESK
description: In 1997, Martha Stewart took over the Skylands estate, diligently preserving its historic architecture and the stunning landscape, initially crafted by Jens Jensen. This remarkable property, once owned by Edsel Ford, encapsulates pivotal elements of American architectural history connected to the Ford lineage. With the help of landscape architect Patrick Chassé, Stewart revitalized the estate’s gardens to harmonize with the natural environment.
title: Martha Stewart bought 63-acre Maine estate for under $6m, restored historic home

author: NILESH BHATTACHARYA
title: For Kolkata’s football fans, Brazil was love before first sight

author: AMIT KUMAR
description: Sujeet Kalkal gave India its first gold medal in wrestling at the Asian Games 2026, winning the men's freestyle 65kg title in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan. Kalkal defeated Tajikistan's Abdulmazhid Kudiev in the final at the Nagoya City Inae Sports Center.
title: Sujeet Kalkal wins India's first wrestling gold at Asian Games 2026

author: YASHASVI VASISTHA
description: Amarinder Singh Raja Warring has suggested his removal from the Punjab Congress chief post is imminent. Internal divisions have prompted calls for leadership change ahead of the 2027 assembly elections. Warring expressed satisfaction with his tenure, despite challenges and differences within the party. Several candidates are being considered to replace him in the upcoming announcement. The party high command will make the final decision on the new leadership.
title: Warring hints at Pilot’s role in Punjab Congress leadership change ahead of 2027 polls

author: TOI BUSINESS DESK
description: The higher speed of 100 kmph was successfully put to the test today, according to Railway minister Ashwini Vaishnaw. Vande Bharat Express (Train No. 26401/26404) set a new record by traversing the world's highest railway bridge, Chenab Bridge, and India's first cable-stayed railway bridge, the Anji Khad Bridge at 100 kmph.
title: Historic milestone: Watch Vande Bharat cross Chenab bridge, Anji bridges at 100 kmph

author: TOI TECH DESK
description: Google has launched its AI chips into space for the first time under Project Suncatcher. A refrigerator-sized Planet Labs satellite carrying four Tensor Processing Units (TPUs) flew aboard SpaceX's Falcon 9 to test whether AI data centres can run in orbit on solar power. The chips will run Google's Gemma AI model in 15-minute bursts, but the company says space-based data centres are at least five years from being cost-effective.
title: Google sends its 'chips' to space in a refrigerator-sized satellite

author: HIJAM RAJU SINGH
description: Ankush Panghal secured the gold medal in the men's 80kg final against South Korea's Minseong Kim. This victory came after Lovlina Borgohain and Parveen Hooda won their respective finals in women's categories. Lovlina celebrated her birthday with a significant win against China's Ziyi Bao, becoming a two-time Asian Games champion. Parveen earned her first Asian Games gold in a tightly contested match against Chen Nien-chin of Chinese Taipei.
title: Three golds in a day! Ankush completes Indian boxing hat-trick at Asian Games

author: PATHIKRIT CHAKRABORTY
description: Dinesh Rai, a private school operator in Kushinagar, was arrested due to a viral video. The video showed him making inappropriate comments to a female staff member. Rai allegedly suggested a physical relationship while referencing personal issues. Following the video's circulation, police registered a case against him under various sections of the law. Further legal action will be determined based on ongoing investigations and available evidence.
title: ‘My wife is ill, I want to sleep with you’: UP school operator's video goes viral

author: G PARTHASARATHY
description: As communal riots raged in 1948, a young Parsi and his friends secretly spirited away a life-size bronze Gandhi statue. Former Indian diplomat G Parthasarathy recounts how one of Pakistan's only two Bapu statues survived.
title: The midnight rescue of Karachi's Mahatma Gandhi

author: TOI ENTERTAINMENT DESK
description: Upasana Singh has voiced concerns over alleged disrespect within the Cine and Television Artistes' Association. She highlighted incidents involving Mukesh Rishi, Deepak Parashar, and Vikas Verma at meetings. Singh described how the treatment of these senior members has led to feelings of humiliation and anger. Allegations against Poonam Dhillon and Padmini Kolhapure indicated a disconnect from other association members due to their status.
title: Upasana Singh alleges Poonam Dhillon, Padmini Kolhapure humiliated senior actors

author: LAIRENLAKPAM WARLI
description: YouTuber Sourav Joshi had an unsettling experience while enjoying time with his family in Haldwani. As he lowered his car window, he expected a warm welcome from a group of men. Unfortunately, the situation took a turn for the worse as they unleashed a tirade of abuse towards him and his family before fleeing the scene.
title: ‘Ye sab nahi chalega’: YouTuber Sourav Joshi chases car after men abuse him, family

author: HIJAM RAJU SINGH
description: Shubman Gill conveyed his strong commitment to addressing unfinished goals in the 2027 ODI World Cup. Recognising the scarcity of opportunities for World Cup participation, he underscored the importance of guidance from seasoned players like Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma. Furthermore, Gill shared that he is prioritising team achievements over personal accolades, viewing captaincy as a pivotal duty rather than a burden.
title: ‘Unfinished business’: Shubman Gill eyes 2027 WC, values Kohli-Rohit experience

author: AADRITA HALDER
title: Thousands stranded in UAE as Israeli rescue flights cancelled over landing clearance

author: ARNAB LALL SEAL
description: Gurinder Singh Sangha has departed from Japan following allegations of sexual misconduct during the Asian Games tournament. Multiple complaints were lodged against him, including inappropriate behavior towards a Malaysian hockey official. He previously faced similar allegations during the Hockey India League in January 2025, leading to a formal complaint by umpire Yogita Pasi.
title: Asian Games hockey official Sangha leaves Japan amid sexual misconduct complaints

author: ARYAN SINGH
description: Amid rising fuel costs, the United States is advocating for European countries to utilize their diesel stockpiles. President Donald Trump is also weighing the option of restricting US diesel exports to safeguard the domestic market. As diesel plays a pivotal role in both transport and agriculture, even minor supply issues can be significant. This situation reveals how international energy dynamics can directly influence homefront economic stability.
title: US weighs diesel export ban, urges Europe to release reserves

author: SHIVANGHI PAYAL
description: Recent declines in gold prices in India have sparked greater interest among physical buyers, leading to reduced discounts from sellers. With the festival season on the horizon, demand is likely to surge, particularly for jewelry. Similarly, Singapore reports increased buying activity, as evidenced by dealer inventories. Meanwhile, China is keeping a close eye on price fluctuations, experiencing high premiums for gold.
title: Gold gets its festive shine back as lower prices lure Asian buyers

author: TOI REAL ESTATE DESK
description: Megan and Jeff Hamann embarked on a creative journey to renovate their kitchen in two distinct phases. With a modest budget of under $10,000, they transitioned their once gaudy space into a charming farmhouse-style kitchen. The initial phase prioritized making the kitchen livable, followed by phase two, which included stylish upgrades like new countertops and lighting fixtures, culminating in a space that's both practical and picturesque.
title: North Dakota couple saved 5 years, then transformed kitchen with $9,037 makeover

author: TOI WORLD DESK
description: An Iowa carpenter who never went to college quietly saved nearly $3 million during his 67-year career. After his death in 2005, the money funded college education for 33 students who could not otherwise afford it. Fourteen years later, the students, known as “Dale’s Kids”, gathered to remember the man they had never met.
title: Iowa carpenter left nearly $3m; 33 students he funded later gathered to honor him

author: TOI SCIENCE DESK
title: Burmese python mothers shiver to heat their eggs in wild Florida nest

author: TOI TECH DESK
description: Elon Musk funded a 25-kilowatt solar project to help a community center in Coden, Alabama. The project was designed to provide electricity during emergencies, ensuring energy safety after disasters. It was installed at the South Bay Communities Alliance Hurricane Response Center, which aided recovery from Hurricane Katrina. SolarCity contributed to the installation and supported Musk's vision for energy independence.
title: In 2010, Elon Musk funded 108 solar panels and battery backup for an Alabama centre

author: TOI REAL ESTATE DESK
title: Dallas extends deadline for $409m Bank of America Plaza redevelopment plan

author: TOI SCIENCE DESK
description: A new restoration strategy has been proposed to address the environmental impacts of the Plymouth Mill in North Carolina. This plan highlights essential actions such as conserving wetlands and restoring natural habitats along the lower Roanoke River. A significant portion, 760 acres of wetlands, will be preserved through a conservation deed. The initiative plans to utilize about $1.
title: North Carolina proposes restoring Roanoke River after 50 years of mill pollution

author: TOI WORLD DESK
description: Terence Kahn, who lived a remarkably simple life, amassed over $13 million before his death in January 2021. After his passing, his estate representatives reached out to various nonprofits in Indianapolis to ensure his wealth was used for good. Among the beneficiaries, Teachers’ Treasures received an impactful donation of $1.6 million, which initiated the nonprofit's inaugural endowment fund and bolstered its mission to distribute essential supplies to teachers.
title: Indianapolis man built $13m fortune; estate gave $1.6m to classroom charity

author: HIJAM RAJU SINGH
description: Lovlina Borgohain celebrated her 29th birthday by winning gold at the Asian Games in Japan. She had previously considered quitting boxing after a disappointing performance at the Paris Olympics. Overcoming self-doubt and a year of challenges, Lovlina triumphed in the women's 75kg final against China's Ziyi Bao. This victory also marked the end of a 12-year wait for a female boxing champion from India.
title: ‘I wanted to quit boxing’: Lovlina fights through tough year to script historic gold

author: TOI BUSINESS DESK
description: On September 17, the government increased the EPFO wage threshold from Rs 15,000 to Rs 25,000. The revision is expected to extend mandatory coverage to more than 10 million additional workers and give another push to workforce formalisation. In the frequently asked questions released on the matter, the ministry acknowledged that the revised wage ceiling would inevitably raise employers' costs.
title: ‘Don’t cut salaries’: Govt’s clear directive to companies as EPF wage ceiling rises

author: TOI TECH DESK
description: In a strategic move, Steve Jobs concealed his Porsche at an investment meeting with Ross Perot, believing that flaunting such wealth might deter interest in NeXT. Conversely, John Ternus proudly showcases his Porsche 935, actively participating in competitive racing. Ternus's passion for motorsports, stemming from his mechanical engineering expertise from the University of Pennsylvania, highlights their contrasting approaches to success and personal expression.
title: Steve Jobs hid his Porsche so NeXT wouldn’t look rich to investors

author: SUDEEP LAVANIA
description: A 25-year-old disciple named Deepak Lodhi allegedly fell from a rooftop, prompting investigations and questioning of residents. CCTV footage shows him sitting on the rooftop before suddenly jumping, raising concerns about the circumstances. The incident has led to significant changes at the ashram, including the suspension of initiation ceremonies and changes to disciples' dress codes. Visitors have reported being unable to meet with Premanand Maharaj due to these restrictions.
title: Mystery shrouds Premanand Maharaj disciple’s death after CCTV emerges

author: LAIRENLAKPAM WARLI
description: The Cockroach Janta Party is gearing up for nationwide protests, beginning in Mumbai, as they call for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. In light of security concerns at Jantar Mantar, twelve Delhi Metro stations' entry and exit gates have been shut down. Despite these restrictions, protesters are anticipated to make their voices heard, according to CJP spokesperson Saurav Das.
title: ‘People will come running’: CJP’s Saurav Das on Delhi Metro station closures

author: KANCHAN YADAV
description: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay launched an expanded scheme to provide free bus travel. Marking the launch on Gandhi Jayanti, Vijay travelled by bus in Chennai and interacted with passengers. The scheme removed previous limitations on the types of bus services available for free travel. It aims to enhance economic empowerment and education opportunities without transportation costs hindering access.
title: Watch: CM Vijay plays bus conductor, hands out tickets after expanding free travel scheme

author: PRANAV SHUKLA
description: With an unbeaten 80 runs, Ishan Kishan played a key role in guiding India to the final of the Asian Games. India's strong performance was underscored by their bowlers, who restricted Sri Lanka to just 45 runs. Kishan recognized the importance of maintaining concentration ahead of the challenging match against Pakistan, acknowledging the intense pressure associated with vying for a medal.
title: 'Not going to be easy': Ishan Kishan ahead of India-Pakistan gold medal clash

author: TOI LIFESTYLE DESK
description: Shashank Agrawal's inspiring journey from a financially challenged background to earning a career package over a crore exemplifies the power of perseverance. After achieving AIR 20 in the JEE Advanced and graduating from IIT Bombay, he is now thriving in the technology and finance sectors. Shashank's story emphasizes hard work and constant improvement, motivating students to believe in their potential despite any obstacles they face.
title: IIT Bombay graduate from Rs 3,000-a-month family lands Rs 1.2 crore package

author: TOI SCIENCE DESK
description: Researchers restored woody habitat along a 110-km section of Australia's Murray River by adding 4,450 timber structures. Over seven years, Murray cod numbers tripled and golden perch numbers doubled in the restored reach, with fish movement from connected source populations also contributing to the increase.
title: Australia restored Murray River with timber; Murray cod abundance tripled

author: DHRUV YADAV
description: The Indian Army has initiated the procurement process for thermal imaging night sights for its medium machine guns. This equipment will allow troops to engage targets effectively from over 1,800 metres, regardless of visibility conditions. Thermal sights detect heat differences, providing an advantage over traditional night-vision systems that rely on ambient light. These sights enhance operational capabilities along challenging terrains and enable surveillance without revealing troop positions.
title: Army seeks thermal sights for machine guns, will help curb infiltration attempts on LoC

author: AADRITA HALDER
title: Karnataka BJP leader booked over alleged bid to delete names of 198 'Muslim voters'

author: TOI TECH DESK
description: BMW will use AI to cut its divisions and management roles by 20% by mid-2027, with similar cuts at lower levels. The carmaker announced the plan at its capital markets day, alongside a margin target of 3% to 5% by 2028. CEO Milan Nedeljkovic said the restructuring will help BMW face fierce competition, as up to 8,000 white-collar jobs in Germany are affected.
title: BMW wants AI to do its managers' jobs, plans 20% layoffs

author: NIKHIL SHARMA
description: In a tragic event on Thursday, authorities apprehended three suspects connected to the gang rape of a 13-year-old girl in Greater Faridabad. Six youths threatened the victims as they returned from tuition classes, leading to the assault in an abandoned structure. After initially hiding the incident, the victims informed their families, resulting in a formal police complaint.
title: Teen gang-raped, her friend sexually assaulted near Delhi

author: PRIYANKA MUKHERJEE
description: Prime Minister Narendra Modi praised Captain Smit Machchhar for courage during a flight emergency involving a co-pilot. Machchhar recited the Hanuman Chalisa to maintain composure while facing danger, which he shared with the Prime Minister. Modi spoke with Machchhar and his family, highlighting his bravery in protecting passengers.
title: 'I was reciting Hanuman Chalisa': flydubai pilot Machchhar tells PM Modi about cockpit ordeal

author: GLOBAL SPORTS DESK
description: Odell Beckham Jr.'s second stint with the New York Giants saw a promising start in preseason, but his impact during regular season was minimal. With only three games played and a mere 19 snaps to his name, Beckham didn't secure any receptions. His release by the team reflects a strategic shift to enhance their offensive lineup, leaving Beckham as a free agent seeking new opportunities.

author: LAIRENLAKPAM WARLI
description: A food delivery worker was filmed urinating in the elevator of Akshay Co-operative Housing Society in Mumbai. Residents noticed a foul smell and checked the CCTV footage, which confirmed the incident. The footage went viral on social media, raising community concerns. Following this, the housing society filed a police complaint against the delivery worker. Also, residents have questioned the verification process for delivery personnel entering their homes.
title: Mumbai delivery worker caught urinating in society lift; CCTV video goes viral

author: HIJAM RAJU SINGH
description: Kumkum Mohod and Dhiraj Bommadevara secured a silver medal in the mixed team recurve event at the Asian Games. The Indian pair fought back from a 0-4 deficit against China's Jingyi Zhu and Mengqi Li, but lost 3-5. Earlier in the semifinals, they staged a remarkable comeback to defeat Japan's Nanami Asakuno and Junya Nakanishi. India's women's recurve team also won gold by defeating South Korea for the first time.
title: Asian Games: Kumkum Mohod, Dhiraj Bommadevara win mixed recurve team silver

author: PRIYANKA JAISWAL
title: ‘Chala chala Shivaji Park’: CJP's Dipke calls on 'sawaris' to join protest against CEC

author: ARYAN SINGH
description: Taiwan is gearing up to strengthen its aerial defenses with the arrival of its first two F-16V fighter jets, marking a significant step in a broader U.S. agreement for 66 aircraft worth roughly $8 billion. These upgraded jets will come equipped with cutting-edge avionics and radar systems, expanding Taiwan's fleet to over 200 F-16s. Despite past delays, more jets are anticipated to arrive before the year's end, amidst ongoing U.S.
title: Taiwan to receive first new F-16 Viper jets from US

author: TOI SCIENCE DESK
description: Researchers utilized fluorescein dye in the Rockall Trough to study deep ocean water upwelling. They measured rapid upward movement reaching about 125 metres per day, significantly faster than average estimates. This study provides direct observations of upwelling in submarines canyons, offering insights into ocean circulation dynamics. Findings suggest underwater topography plays a crucial role in deep-water circulation processes. Future research aims to explore similar processes in different submarine canyon settings.
title: Scientists tracked deep-sea dye; canyon water rose 100 metres a day

author: TOI WORLD DESK
description: Kōkua Hawaiʻi Foundation acquired unused farmland on Oʻahu in 2019 to create an educational resource. Over six years, more than 40,000 pounds of produce were harvested while 2,200 students participated in learning experiences. The farm emphasizes ecological education, agroforestry, and understanding local food systems through hands-on activities. Community involvement plays a significant role in maintaining the farm through regular volunteer opportunities.
title: Jack Johnson’s Hawaii farm harvested over 40,000 pounds of produce in six years

author: SAURABH THAKUR
description: A couple in Delhi alleged unfair practices by Royalty Holidays International after purchasing a holiday membership. They were misled about benefits and terms during a promotional event, leading to a complaint. The consumer commission found the company guilty of unfair trade practices and deficient service. They mandated Royalty Holidays to refund the couple's payment, along with additional compensation for their distress.
title: Free hotel stays promised, Delhi couple signs Rs 65k membership; court orders relief

author: PRANAV SHUKLA
description: Rishabh Pant has not donned the ODI jersey for India in more than two years, leaving his international career in limbo. Although he has shone in Test matches, fierce competition for the wicketkeeper role in ODIs and T20s looms large. After a year lost to injury, players like KL Rahul have seized their chance.
title: 'You feel bad': Rishabh Pant breaks silence on losing India ODI spot to KL Rahul

title: EC launches special drive to restore names dropped during SIR

author: TOI BUSINESS DESK
description: Under Section 56(2)(x), there is applicable taxation of such a difference in the buyer's hands if the stamp duty value of the property is higher than the purchase consideration by more than the greater of Rs 50,000 or 10% of the consideration.  Here, the difference of approximately Rs 22.71 lakh exceeded 10% of the agreed purchase price of Rs 1.23 crore.
title: Property value rose before registration; ITAT scraps Rs 11.35 lakh tax on buyer

author: TOI TECH DESK
description: Ford's CEO Jim Farley emphasized that artificial intelligence will complement skilled trades workers, assuring that roles requiring hands-on skills and practical judgment are safe despite AI advancements. He pointed out that fostering trust is crucial for the successful collaboration between workers and AI. Additionally, he noted the merging roles of tradespeople and engineers in contemporary manufacturing, showcasing Ford's evolution in job functions to adapt to technology.

author: HIJAM RAJU SINGH
description: Lovlina Borgohain made history by clinching a gold medal at the Asian Games, becoming just the second Indian woman boxer to achieve this feat. She delivered an impressive performance, sweeping the finals against China's Ziyi Bao with a perfect 5-0 score. This triumph comes after her silver medal in the last Asian Games, where her journey was highlighted by a semifinal win against world champion Natalya Bogdanova.
title: Birthday girl Lovlina makes history with gold, joins Mary Kom in elite club

title: PM Modi speaks to India's 'hero' flydubai pilot Smit Machchhar, wishes him quick recovery

title: Somerset family grows same broad bean since 1875; heirloom joins national collection

author: GLOBAL SPORTS DESK
description: Cristiano Ronaldo grew up in a small home in Madeira, sharing his space with three siblings. He pursued his football talent, moving to Lisbon to join Sporting CP at 12 years old. After reaching prominence in football, he built a mansion in Cascais, valued between €30 million and €35 million. Despite its luxury, he chose to sell it soon after completion to seek more privacy.
title: From modest Madeira home to $30M palace: Cristiano Ronaldo's journey

author: SRISHTI LAKHOTIA
description: The Calcutta High Court has rejected a woman's request concerning her husband's potential deportation over absent identification documents. The court expressed concerns about the husband's capability to demonstrate his Indian nationality during ongoing investigations. Detained since August 31 on suspicions of illegal immigration from Bangladesh, his legal team contends that the detention is unjustified, as he has not been formally charged. Authorities have mandated the submission of his citizenship documentation.
title: Prove you are Indian, Calcutta HC tells SIR-deleted ‘Bangladeshi’

author: SHIVANGHI PAYAL
description: Stock trading will be halted on October 2, 2026, in observance of Mahatma Gandhi Jayanti. Both the National Stock Exchange and Bombay Stock Exchange will be closed for the day, along with the Multi Commodity Exchange. Investors have faced declines for four consecutive sessions, impacted by foreign selling and escalating crude oil prices. The trading schedule will also be affected by the upcoming Dussehra and Diwali holidays.
title: Gandhi Jayanti: Are NSE, BSE closed for trading on October 2?

author: ARYAN SINGH
description: India's Akash air defence missile system has been successfully exported to Tajikistan and Turkmenistan. This follows the initial export to Armenia, marking significant international expansion. The Akash system is designed to protect areas from aerial threats and has a proven operational record. Additionally, the Indian armed forces are placing more orders and potential international demand is expected. The growth of India's defence exports reflects its advancing missile production capabilities.
title: India's defence export milestone: Akash air defence missile enters Central Asia

author: ISHITA JAIRATH
description: Delhi's recent opening of the Barapullah Phase III corridor has resulted in significant traffic congestion for commuters. Thousands of drivers expected a quick journey but faced extended delays beyond two hours. Traffic Police are examining the corridor's design and lane configurations to improve flow. They are considering temporary measures such as barricades and traffic regulation adjustments. Further analysis includes addressing navigation app routing to better manage traffic conditions.
title: 2 days on, Ph-3 chaos throws up design flaws in entire Barapullah

author: SABI HUSSAIN
description: At the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, India has witnessed a notable drop in gold medals, plummeting from 28 in Hangzhou to merely 10 this time around. Key defeats were recorded in shooting, athletics, and team events, stirring concerns about future prospects. However, the men's hockey and cricket finals still present a chance to hold onto some glory, prompting reflection on how India can reclaim its previous success in sports.
title: India’s Asian Games gold slide: 20 of 28 Hangzhou titles already lost

author: SHIVANGHI PAYAL
description: Recent developments have led to a surge in oil prices, largely driven by new restrictions placed on Chinese fuel exports. This, combined with reports of increased US military presence in the Middle East, has heightened concerns over supply stability. Following the escalation of conflict between the US and Israel regarding Iran, both Brent and WTI crude prices have risen sharply.

author: PRATYUSH RAJ
description: Simranjit Singh a.k.a Simi Singh left left India in 2006 to pursue hotel management, found an unexpected second career in cricket, played for Ireland at the 2022 T20 World Cup and then survived acute liver failure. Now, after his wife donated part of her liver to save him, Simi Singh has returned home to Mohali, bringing a remarkable 20-year journey to an end. Yet, his association with cricket will continue: he's opened an academy, where he is honing young talent.
title: Simi Singh: An Ireland dream, a life-threatening detour and the journey home

title: Putin warns West of 'all weapons' use if Russia’s exclave Kaliningrad is attacked

author: GLOBAL SPORTS DESK
description: Micah Hyde didn't hold back in criticizing Tom Brady and Rob Gronkowski's presence during a Bills game broadcast. He revealed his unease about their involvement, remembering their past victories over the Bills. Specifically, Hyde stated he didn't want to see Brady at Highmark Stadium, emphasizing the intense rivalry between the Patriots and Bills. Regardless of the broadcast, the Bills triumphed against the Chargers that night.
title: Tom Brady-Rob Gronkowski FOX controversy reignites as Micah Hyde revives rivalry

author: PRANAV SHUKLA
description: India made history as its women's recurve archery team bagged the inaugural gold medal at the Asian Games, defeating the formidable South Korean squad, known for their ten Olympic golds, with a tight score of 5-3. The final was a nail-biter, with both teams demonstrating exceptional prowess amidst blustery weather. This landmark win comes after a thrilling semifinal against China, underscoring the team's exceptional talent and tenacity.
title: Gold medal secured! India’s women recurve archers defeat South Korea in final

author: TOI LIFESTYLE DESK
description: Children frequently engage in imaginative play with their toys, using dialogue to enhance their language skills and social interactions. By directing these scenarios, they explore a range of emotions and relationships. Studies suggest that using private speech while playing is linked to improved self-regulation and communication abilities. As they engage in these playful activities, children develop essential skills that translate into their everyday conversations.
title: Kids who whisper to toys are practising key real-life skill, psychology says

author: TOI SCIENCE DESK
description: The Moab Uranium Mill Tailings Remedial Action Project has efficiently relocated 17 million tons of waste from the riverbank. Following rail transportation, teams are actively monitoring groundwater contamination levels. Upcoming efforts will also involve excavating contaminated soil near the original tailings site. The objective is to guarantee long-term safety and stability for local residents and the ecosystem. Ultimately, regrading and revegetating the area will be crucial in preventing future erosion.
title: Utah removes 17 million tons of radioactive waste from beside Colorado River

author: RAJEEV SINGH
description: The San Francisco-based artificial intelligence company did not publicly identify the researchers, but the Wall Street Journal and Bloomberg reported that they were Jasmine Wang, Tomek Korbak and Mikita Balesni. At least two of them worked on AI safety and alignment, areas focused on making advanced AI systems behave safely and follow human instructions. "We have parted ways with three individuals," OpenAI told news agency AFP in a statement.
title: OpenAI fires 3 researchers as AI safety concerns intensify across tech industry

title: Cornell sexual assault case: Snapchat records, police transcript prompt fresh probe

author: ARYAN SINGH
description: The US military has deployed extra Patriot missile batteries to Saudi Arabia and Qatar to enhance regional security. This move aims to protect critical oil and gas facilities against potential Iranian attacks. Concerns were raised by Saudi and Qatari leaders regarding Iran's potential retaliation amidst escalating tensions. Moreover, the Pentagon is increasing military presence in the Middle East, deploying additional warships and troops.
title: Gulf oil infrastructure at risk as US rushes Patriot missiles to Saudi Arabia, Qatar

author: TOI TECH DESK
description: Mark Zuckerberg significantly influenced an AI agreement forged between major tech firms and the White House. The pact seeks to implement strong internal controls and outside audits for frontier AI models. Zuckerberg's discussions with key industry executives and lawmakers facilitated the creation of this collaborative document. The agreement does not impose legal requirements but suggests potential future federal regulation on AI.
title: White House AI accord hailed as ‘historic concord’ may have Mark Zuckerberg’s ‘stamp’

author: SHIVANGHI PAYAL
description: India and the US are nearing the final stages of a significant trade agreement, with expectations of its announcement imminent. US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer revealed that teams are actively working through residual challenges. Union Minister Piyush Goyal engaged in talks with Greer during the G20 Trade Ministers' Meeting to expedite the deal. A forthcoming call between PM Modi and President Trump is likely to evaluate the progress.
title: India-US trade deal not imminent, PM Modi-Trump may hold another call soon: US trade rep

author: TNN
description: Social media users worldwide are praising Captain Smit Machchhar for his bravery in saving passengers. People are urging the government to consider him for prestigious civilian awards, highlighting his acts of heroism. Residents from Ghatkopar are expressing pride as they share his background and achievements. Many shared his 2025 podcast discussing the importance of having doctors on flights in emergencies.
title: 'Proud of our Mumbai boy': Netizens hail flydubai hero pilot, seek Ashok Chakra

author: TOI WORLD DESK
description: Ray Vetuskey, 64, is marking the 100th birthday of the kidney his mother donated to him when he was 16. The transplant, performed in 1978, has survived far beyond the typical 15–20 years. Doctors expect the kidney to last for life, while Vetuskey remains Strong Memorial Hospital’s longest-surviving kidney transplant recipient.
title: Man marks 100th birthday of kidney donated by mom 48 years ago

author: TOI ENTERTAINMENT DESK
description: Mammootty's former residence in Kochi's Panampilly Nagar has opened its doors to fans as a unique holiday accommodation. This charming villa offers four distinctive bedrooms, welcoming up to eight guests. In addition to the cozy sleeping arrangements, guests can indulge in a private theatre and art galleries during their stay. The entire villa can be booked for around Rs 25,433, exclusive of taxes.
title: Mammootty's Panampilly Nagar house is now a stay

author: JYOTIRMOY HALDER
description: Welcome to TimesofIndia.com's interview series looking back at India's medal-winning campaigns at the Chess Olympiad in Samarkand. After kicking things off with Srinath Narayanan and India's silver-winning Open team, we turn to Swayams Mishra, captain of the bronze-winning women's team. In an exclusive interaction, the 34-year-old opens up about his first full stint as captain, the difficult decision-making around Vaishali, Savitha Shri's match-winning impact, and much more.
title: ‘If India won a medal, we owe it to her’: Captain Swayams on Savitha's heroics

author: ARYAN SINGH
description: In a significant escalation of the conflict, Ukraine has confirmed its inaugural deployment of the FP-7 tactical ballistic missile, a cutting-edge weapon designed by Fire Point. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy disclosed this news on October 1 via Telegram. While details regarding the missile's target and effects are currently classified, the FP-7 boasts an impressive range of about 250 kilometers.
title: Ukraine claims first combat use of its home-made ballistic missile against Russia

author: AADRITA HALDER
title: 'He has good ideas': Putin lauds PM Modi's peace push to end Russia-Ukraine war

author: TOI WORLD DESK
description: In a significant move towards sustainability, over 120 acres of Hoyt Farm in Essex have been shielded from commercial development, safeguarding its agricultural, forestry, and wildlife heritage. With cultivation practices dating back two centuries, this initiative, driven by local leaders and state agencies, secures essential natural resources and bolsters community food security, all while optimizing financial support to minimize town burden.
title: 100-year Massachusetts family farm preserved in 120-acre conservation deal

author: TOI SCIENCE DESK
description: Archaeologists have recovered remarkably preserved worked wood dating back 10,500 years from beneath Germany’s Lake Arendsee. The finds include a 1.6-metre post with felling marks and split boards up to 1.3 metres long. Researchers believe they may be remnants of Mesolithic huts or previously unknown structures, offering new insights into hunter-gatherer life.
title: 10,500-year-old wood found 20m deep in Germany's Lake Arendsee

author: TOI WORLD DESK
description: A 255-year-old mansion, Galloway House, was moved by a Maryland family to prevent it from being demolished. The structure traveled approximately 50 miles across the Chesapeake Bay after extensive planning and specialized equipment. Crews lifted the 400-ton house for a phased relocation that began in September 2019. After arriving at its new waterfront property in Queenstown, restoration efforts commenced to preserve its historic character.
title: Family moves 255-year-old mansion 50 miles by barge across Chesapeake Bay

author: MIHIR TANKSALE, SANDIP DIGHE, GEORGE MENDONCA
description: A tragic incident occurred at Diveagar beach where eight students from Alandi drowned during a picnic. The students ventured into the sea despite warnings from their teachers and some not knowing how to swim. Local water sports club workers quickly responded to the emergency after being alerted by others on the beach. The bodies were recovered and taken to a nearby hospital where they were declared dead.
title: ‘Told them not to go deep’: How picnic trip turned deadly for eight 16-year-old boys

author: TOI WORLD DESK
description: Comfort Cases, founded by Rob Scheer in 2013, helps provide essential items for children entering foster care. After experiencing the trauma of carrying trash bags, Scheer initiated a movement to change this narrative. The organization has distributed over 300,000 bags across multiple regions, including the US and the UK. It continually collaborates with community organizations to reach children in need effectively.
title: Ex-foster kid's charity donates 300,000+ backpacks to children

author: TOI WORLD DESK
description: A Leeds mum says her £217,000 dream home became a four-year nightmare after her neighbour demolished his half of their semi-detached property. She claims the work left her £80,000-renovated home exposed to rain, damp, mould and vermin. The neighbour disputes responsibility, while Leeds City Council says the property remains structurally stable and continues monitoring the site.
title: Leeds mum's £217k home left exposed as neighbour demolishes half of semi

author: PATHIKRIT CHAKRABORTY
description: In Lucknow, a 17-year-old allegedly killed his 42-year-old mother following an argument about gender-affirming surgery. The minor had been living as a female and wanted to undergo surgery. An altercation reportedly arose when the mother advised against the procedure. The teenager attacked her with an iron wrench, resulting in fatal injuries. He subsequently informed the police about the incident himself.
title: Uttar Pradesh teen kills his mother for opposing sex change

author: TNN
description: The Gujarat government has taken disciplinary action leading to the compulsory retirement of two IAS officers. Kankipati Rajesh faces ongoing corruption and money-laundering investigations by CBI and ED since 2022. Gaurav Dahiya was suspended in 2019 over allegations of misconduct, including bigamy and cheating. Both officers were deemed unsuitable for service based on their reviewed records by the Department of Personnel and Training.
title: 'Unsuitable for service': 2 Gujarat IAS officers forced into retirement
